subject.title: fix(mcp): bind stored OAuth refresh token to its issuer

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally require one-time reauthorization for Doctor-imported MCP OAuth token-only rows once discovery occurs, because their issuer cannot be safely reconstructed?
rationale: The secure behavior is a deliberate compatibility change for existing imported credentials; source evidence cannot determine whether maintainers want to accept that interruption or define a separately recoverable migration contract.

options.title: Accept fail-closed reauthorization
options.body: Merge the issuer guard and require a fresh `openclaw mcp login` for token-only legacy rows after discovery, preventing cross-issuer refresh-token replay.

options.title: Define a recoverable migration contract
options.body: Pause for a maintainer-approved source of issuer provenance that can be verified without exposing legacy refresh tokens to newly discovered issuers.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed reauthorization
recommendation.body: Merge the issuer guard and require a fresh `openclaw mcp login` for token-only legacy rows after discovery, preventing cross-issuer refresh-token replay.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged SQLite MCP OAuth migration owns the relevant persisted credential and Doctor-import boundary.
